cards.title: IBM Granite 4.2: 3B/8B/30B Reasoning LLMs with 512K Context, Agentic RL, Apache 2.0
cards.why_it_matters: Granite 4.2 is a fully open-weight reasoning family with agentic RL training and a 512K context window — directly relevant for researchers building or benchmarking capable, deployable open models.
cards.summary: Granite 4.2 releases three dense decoder-only models (3B, 8B, 30B) pretrained from scratch on ~15T tokens across five phases, reaching 512K context. All three get SFT on chain-of-thought and tool-use data (~7.2M samples, ~100B tokens), then multi-stage RL. The 8B and 30B additionally undergo agentic RL in sandboxed environments with code execution, terminal, and web tools. All support thinking/non-thinking/low-effort modes, native tool calling in OpenAI format, and Apache 2.0 licensing.

cards.title: Gradio's gr.Workflow: Graph-Based AI Pipeline Builder with Auto-REST API and HF Spaces Deploy
cards.why_it_matters: Directly lowers the overhead for ML engineers to expose multi-step model pipelines as both interactive UIs and REST endpoints, with parallel fan-out and GPU support built in.
cards.summary: gr.Workflow, built into Gradio, lets developers define multi-step AI pipelines as typed node graphs supporting Python functions, Hugging Face Inference Providers, other Gradio Spaces, or Hub datasets. The same graph renders as a drag-and-drop canvas and auto-generates named REST endpoints per output node. Fan-out parallel execution, ZeroGPU integration for on-demand GPU access, and one-command deployment to HF Spaces are all included.

cards.title: FraudBench: Protocol Choice Swings Feasible Adversarial Examples from 3.7 to 2,832 in Financial ML Robustness Eval
cards.why_it_matters: Highlights a fundamental evaluation pitfall — protocol sensitivity — that applies broadly to any ML robustness benchmark using domain constraints, not just financial fraud detection.
cards.summary: FraudBench evaluates the same dataset–model–attack–defense configurations under three protocols: unconstrained attacks, post-hoc feasibility filtering, and constraint-integrated attacks. On Lending Club Loan Data under white-box settings, post-hoc filtering yields ~3.7 feasible-flipped examples on average, while constraint-integrated attack generation produces ~2,832.3 under the same budget. On IEEE-CIS, feasibility and attacker capability emerge as independent axes; black-box protocol choice also alters model-family rankings.

cards.title: Neurosymbolic Alignment: HGNN Physiological World Model Drives ORPO to 90.8% Clinical Safety Score, Beating GPT-4 5-shot
cards.why_it_matters: The framework of grounding preference optimization with a structured knowledge-graph scorer is technically transferable beyond clinical AI to any domain where symbolic constraints should shape RLHF/preference training.
cards.summary: A 7B clinical LLM is coupled with an HGNN-based Physiological World Model over an 847K-node biomedical knowledge graph. Candidate responses are scored via homeostatic constraints, multi-hop path plausibility, and drug-interaction penalties; scores drive iterative on-policy ORPO updates. On the 2,500-scenario Clinical Safety Benchmark, CSS improves from 69.5% to 90.8% (+21.3 pp over ORPO), harmful-response rate drops from 14.1% to 5.1%, and drug-interaction detection improves from 72.8% to 91.6%. The method exceeds GPT-4 5-shot on all safety metrics and outperforms SFT+SelfCorrect by 11.4 pp CSS.

cards.title: PeakBench: New Benchmark Disentangles Logical Dependency Planning from Resource-Constrained Scheduling in LLM Tool Agents
cards.why_it_matters: Addresses a concrete gap in agent evaluation — most benchmarks ignore parallel execution safety under resource constraints — directly relevant for researchers building or evaluating production LLM agents.
cards.summary: PeakBench provides executable multi-tool workflows with dependency annotations and measured resource profiles, targeting the gap between logical planning (tool selection, argument generation) and physical scheduling (parallelization under resource limits). Its two-part evaluation framework isolates each dimension with dedicated metrics. Results show strong logical planning does not reliably yield safe or efficient execution under resource constraints, and that exposing resource information reduces avoidable overflows.

cards.title: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH): 4-bit Compressed 60B Model Beats Its bfloat16 Checkpoint on 7 of 9 Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: QAH inverts the standard accuracy hierarchy between quantized and full-precision models, offering a principled distillation recipe for researchers working on efficient LLM deployment after structural compression.
cards.summary: QAH distills a structurally compressed, MXFP4-quantized student (60B parameters) directly from the original full-size, full-precision teacher via KL divergence on logits, bypassing the degraded recovered bfloat16 checkpoint used in standard quantization-aware distillation. Applied to a GPT-OSS 120B model compressed to 60B and quantized to MXFP4, the 4-bit student outperforms the bfloat16 checkpoint on 7 of 9 benchmarks. KL distillation also provides training stability absent from cross-entropy task losses.

cards.title: StrokeGuard: Dual-Agent System for Prehospital FAST Stroke Screening on Mobile Devices
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a practical multi-agent architecture with state-machine control and stage-local fallback — a concrete systems pattern relevant to agentic AI design beyond healthcare.
cards.summary: StrokeGuard separates formal FAST assessment (facial palsy, arm weakness, speech impairment) from procedural support using a dual-channel agent mechanism with state-machine control and stage-local fallback recovery. Video assessment modules handle per-stage scoring. In a simulated prehospital scenario, it improved MATES-9 user-experience scores by 10.83 points (23.8% relative increase) over a paper FAST-style form.

cards.title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search Discovers Transmission Protocols Boosting Collective Problem-Solving by up to 37%
cards.why_it_matters: Using LLMs to evolve state-aware coordination protocols is a frontier application of AI-assisted algorithm design relevant to researchers working on multi-agent systems and collective intelligence.
cards.summary: The paper formalizes information-sharing protocols as state-aware programs that route resources based on agent and collective states, going beyond fixed network topologies. LLM-guided evolutionary search discovers protocols for a collective discovery task, improving performance over standard baselines by up to 37%. Ablations show that removing content-dependence while preserving network topology eliminates performance gains, confirming state-awareness as the key driver. Evolved protocols transfer across domain variations and agent populations.

cards.title: LumiXAI: Modular Full-Stack Framework Unifying Feature Attribution Across Modalities, APIs, and GUIs
cards.why_it_matters: Interpretability tooling fragmentation slows research iteration; a unified, extensible framework with plug-in attribution methods and containerized reproducibility is a practical infrastructure gain for ML engineers.
cards.summary: LumiXAI consolidates feature attribution into a single system with classification and generative attribution, an interactive GUI for bidirectional exploration, and a plug-in architecture for adding models and methods. Three access tiers serve non-programmers, developers, and extenders from one backend. Containerized services and persistent result storage are designed to make attribution analyses reproducible across machines.
